close_reason: Fused public tuple construction returns canonical bottom on an uninhabited field with no extra pass; the TDD proof records no interner work.
description:
Goal: Return canonical bottom from public tuple construction when an already-interned tuple field is the canonical bottom Ty, without adding a second traversal to ordinary tuple construction.

Signal: `Types::tuple` always built a tuple descriptor and entered `Types::intern`; the existing type tests prove `tuple([int, none]) = none`. A red interning-work test for an interior `none` field measured one raw index probe, one full normalization, and one canonical-index probe for this known-empty product.

Strategy: Fuse the shallow canonical-bottom check into the one field-copy pass `Types::tuple` already needs. Return `none` as soon as a field handle is bottom; otherwise pass the exact completed field vector into the descriptor builder. Keep descriptor emptiness for arbitrary descriptors that have no Ty and do not add a hash/cache or a pre-scan.

TDD: Assert an interior bottom coordinate yields semantic bottom with no interning work. Exercise type algebra and the enum/f98 canaries.

Docs and acceptance: Document the product-factor law and the no-extra-pass constraint. Run focused type and enum/f98 canaries, fmt, check, strict Clippy, full workspace tests, cold branch-base review, one commit, and close.
title: Return impossible tuple construction before descriptor normalization
